column1: # Security closure ledger. Verified by scripts/check-closures.sh, which fails
# the build if a named test does not exist, or does not produce a literal
# `--- PASS: <name>` line in the environment its own verification column

column7: note

column1: #   default-ci   the proving test runs and passes in every invocation of this
#                script, no special environment required. A SKIP here is
#   pg-gated     the proving test is gated behind KEYORIX_TEST_PG_DSN (a race
#                that can only be demonstrated against a real multi-connection
#                script runs WITHOUT the DSN set (its default invocation, in
#                the adr-numbers job), a SKIP here is expected and does NOT
#                fail the check — there is nothing else that invocation could
#                show. When it runs WITH the DSN set (.github/workflows/ci.yml
#                test-suite job, `core` leg — the one job with a Postgres
#                service container — runs this same script a second time, see
#                that job for why), a SKIP or failure here IS real and DOES
#                fail the check: the DSN is available, so "gated" stops being
#                an excuse. The test's plain EXISTENCE (a real compiled test
#                symbol, not a typo'd/renamed/deleted name) is checked
#                unconditionally either way — a SKIP line only ever appears
#                for a test that exists and ran; "no tests to run" is the
#   manual       no automated regression test exists or can exist for this
#                claim; closure rests on a cited artefact instead. `note` MUST
#                cite the artefact precisely enough that a skeptical reader
#                could go look (a file path + line, a PR review comment URL, a
#                dated manual test log — not "verified manually" on its own).
#                This is an ESCAPE HATCH, not a shortcut: "self-reported
#                verification is a claim, not evidence" applies in full here —
#                CI accepts the row because it is honestly labeled unverified,
#                not because anything was proven. Prefer default-ci or
#                pg-gated whenever a real test is possible.
# issue is the GitHub issue number this closes (bare, no '#'), or `-` when the
# claim is an internal structural invariant with no single corresponding issue
# (e.g. G01, INV-1) or the note already cites more than one ambiguously
# (FIX-4-sentinel). This column is best-effort cross-referenced by
# the `security` label — read that script's own header before trusting its
# silence: the label it keys off is empirically under-applied (verified
# 2026-09-08 — #1646, #1780, #1551, and #1572 all carry ZERO labels, including
# the two rows already correctly in this ledger before this column existed),
# so a `-` here or an issue missing from that report's output is not proof
# landed_commit is INFORMATIONAL. This repo squash-merges, so ancestry checks
# return false for every correctly landed PR. Closure is verified by test.

column7: project-scoped group membership must not grant cross-project secret read
last-admin refused at the primitive, not only at entry points
the SSO path must not bypass the group guards
cross-tenant credential revoke must be refused
deactivation must not leave tokens live
#1668/#1669 sentinel must survive adjacent commits
reentrancy guard keys on lockKey, not "any lock held"
403/404 split must not be an existence oracle
purge must not hard-delete a row mid-reconciliation
structural: every CSV writer applies an encoder
structural: every direct role grant checks authority
unpinned gcp-secret-manager connector must refuse reads, not span any GCP project
pinned aws-secrets-manager connector must refuse an ARN naming a different AWS account
TPM/cloud-KMS wrapped-KEK blob must be covered by the shared key-permission checker registry, not just DEK/salt
IsGlobalAdmin's PAT short-circuit answered a third-party question it wasn't built for; guardLastAdminDeactivation and SuspendInactiveUsers now use targetHasGlobalAdminRole instead
SoD direct-grant race across independent Postgres connections: two replicas each pass a stale pre-grant check and both write, live-reproduced; closed by WithNamedLock keyed per target principal

SoD group-grant race: a group-role grant and a direct grant to one of its members took different lock keys and never serialized against each other; closed by taking each active member's own lock, ordered, before the group grant's check-then-write

Render's guard only blocked newline/CR/NUL, not shell metacharacters ($(...), backticks, ;|&), enabling RCE if a rendered .env was later sourced; re-verified 2026-09-09 with an end-to-end source attempt
runLogin auto-filled the remote server from an untrusted CWD-relative keyorix.yaml with no warning before sending the real API key; re-verified 2026-09-09 via httptest reproduction

InitializeApp() fmt.Println'd the entire config.Config struct (DB password, metrics tokens) to stdout; re-verified 2026-09-09, and the only caller (cmd/secret) was separately deleted as dead code in PR #1659

runUpdate's embedded-mode path bypassed at-rest AES-256-GCM encryption by calling a raw storage/core constructor instead of common.InitializeCoreService(); re-verified 2026-09-09 with red-then-green against the pre-#1395 vulnerable shape

create.go's runCreate had no common.NewRemoteClient() guard, so a keyorix connect-configured operator running share create from a directory with a local keyorix.yaml would silently write to the local embedded DB instead of the remote server; re-verified 2026-09-09 red-then-green against the pre-#1395 unguarded shape

create.go/update.go/revoke.go passed a literal 1 as SharedBy/UpdatedBy/revokedBy instead of the real acting actor, defeating sharing.go's requireLiveOwnerAuthority ownership gate for whichever user held ID 1; re-verified 2026-09-09 red-then-green against the pre-#G67 hardcoded-actor shape

runAssignRoleToGroup's embedded-mode path called st.AssignRoleToGroup directly, bypassing core.KeyorixCore's requireGroupGrantNoSoDViolation separation-of-duties gate; verified 2026-09-09 with red-then-green against the pre-#1395 raw-storage shape

runRemoveRoleFromGroup's embedded-mode path called st.RemoveRoleFromGroup directly, bypassing core.KeyorixCore's guardLastGlobalAdminGroupRole last-global-admin lockout; verified 2026-09-09 with red-then-green against the pre-#1395 raw-storage shape

DeleteSecret handler (server/http/handlers/secrets_crud.go) unconditionally routed through the per-user owner/sharing permission check (userID != 0 required), so any machine-identity-authenticated caller got a misleading 500 on every delete regardless of the route's own scoped-permission gate; sibling handlers (GetSecret/GetSecretByName/GetSecretValueByRef) already had the correct isMachine bypass, DeleteSecret was the one call site missing it; found by the #1808 tranche-2 differential conformance harness, fixed same commit

AzureKeyVaultConnector's client had no CheckRedirect override, so it followed a cross-host 301/302/303/307/308 redirect and trusted the redirected response as the secret value (credentials confirmed not to leak, but the response content was); found by response-fuzz harness construction, fixed by hardened_client.go's refuseRedirect wired into azurekv.go's client(); see docs/findings/2026-09-19-FINDING-connect-response-trust-gaps.md §2

AWSSecretsManagerConnector had no response-size bound; a gzip-bombed backend response (~2 MiB compressed) forced ~4 GiB peak heap via transparent decompression with err=nil; fixed by hardened_client.go's sizeCappedRoundTripper capping the decompressed body at connectMaxResponseBytes; see docs/findings/2026-09-19-FINDING-connect-response-trust-gaps.md §3

AzureKeyVaultConnector had no response-size bound; the same gzip-bomb shape forced ~3.6 GiB peak heap with err=nil; fixed the same way as the AWS sibling, wired into azurekv.go's client() via azsecrets.ClientOptions.Transport; see docs/findings/2026-09-19-FINDING-connect-response-trust-gaps.md §3

Vault and Azure Key Vault connectors accepted a link-local configured Address (including cloud IMDS, 169.254.169.254) with no rejection at registration or dial time; fixed by validateConnectorAddressNotLinkLocal (registration, literal-IP case) plus connectGuardedDialer's netutil.Dialer{Disallow: netutil.IsLinkLocal} (every dial, including a hostname resolving to link-local); deliberately narrower than a full private-range block -- general RFC-1918/on-prem addresses stay unguarded, the on-prem deployment baseline; see docs/findings/2026-09-19-FINDING-connect-response-trust-gaps.md §2/§5

IsLinkLocal (the narrower SSRF-target check used by the JWKS/OIDC egress guard and now internal/connect's hardened transport) did not decode NAT64 (64:ff9b::/96) or IPv4-compatible (::x) IPv6 encodings of an embedded link-local IPv4 -- only IsPrivateOrLinkLocal had that decode step (#1937/ssrf-nat64-ipv4compat-001); a NAT64-encoded cloud IMDS target would pass IsLinkLocal despite IsPrivateOrLinkLocal already rejecting it. Fixed by refactoring both predicates onto one shared matchesCIDRsWithEmbedded helper; found while implementing the Connect hardened-client link-local guard, which needed IsLinkLocal to have the same coverage IsPrivateOrLinkLocal already did

commitNewKEKFiles' rename-dek error cleanup unconditionally deleted kek.salt.pending on ANY rename error, without checking whether the rename had actually applied first (e.g. an NFS lost-reply/retransmit ambiguity) -- orphaning the DEK (every secret undecryptable) whenever it had. Fixed by dekRenameActuallySucceeded verifying actual on-disk content before cleanup; found by FuzzFaultInjectedOperations same PR as the fix (docs/findings/2026-09-19-FINDING-kek-rotation-rename-dek-cleanup-dataloss.md). landed_commit is a placeholder pending this branch's actual merge commit

column7: ParseResponse accepted a validly-signed response with bytes appended after its root element (XML epilogue) unrejected by either our own XML-DSig path or crewjam/saml's internal xrv.Validate (token-round-trip check, not document-structure check); found by the new FuzzParseResponse harness (#1889) on day one, fixed same PR via validatePostedResponseHasNoEpilogue

IsPrivateOrLinkLocal (shared SSRF blocklist for dynamic-secrets admin-DSN dials, Azure KMS dials, validateAdminDSNHost) accepted NAT64 (64:ff9b::/96) and IPv4-compatible (::x) IPv6 encodings of private/loopback/IMDS IPv4 (e.g. 64:ff9b::a9fe:a9fe = IMDS 169.254.169.254); To4 folds only IPv4-mapped. Fixed by decoding the embedded IPv4 and checking it (not a wholesale-prefix block, so public NAT64 egress is preserved); found by adversarial probe building the DSN SSRF fuzzer, locked by FuzzIPv4EmbeddingSSRFParity (#1937)

serveAuthCacheHit's session branch only re-checked the owning account's state, never whether the session row itself still existed -- RevokeUserSessions and 6 sibling call sites (ChangePassword, ActivateMFA/DisableMFA, WebAuthn enrollment/removal, both setup-token-consume paths, the /system proxy's DeleteSessionsForUserExcept) could leave a deleted session authenticating via a stale positive cache entry; fixed by core.SessionLiveForToken wired into serveAuthCacheHit; found by FuzzConcurrentOpsLinearizable, landed same PR; see docs/findings/2026-09-20-FINDING-session-revoke-cache-race.md

the same session-liveness chokepoint closes the ADR-039-documented cross-replica cache-staleness bound (a revoke on one replica leaving the session live on another for up to validTokenTTL) down to the next request, since SessionLiveForToken re-reads from the same shared DB every replica already writes to; two cores sharing one DB, only one with the cache invalidator wired, prove a replica that never heard about a sibling's revoke still denies on its next cache hit; see docs/findings/2026-09-20-FINDING-session-revoke-cache-race.md

AccountLoginBlocked and AccountRestricted are not the same predicate (pending_first_login/password_reset_required are restricted but not login-blocked) -- a session cache hit's pre-existing account-usability check only re-verified the login-blocked boolean, never refreshed the cached AccountState/Restricted, so a transition into a restricted-but-not-blocked state (e.g. an admin's RequirePasswordReset) stayed invisible to EnforceAccountRestriction on a cache hit; fixed by core.AccountUsabilityAndState / cloneUserContextWithAccountState; see docs/findings/2026-09-20-FINDING-session-revoke-cache-race.md
